exercise.name: Resistance Band Standing Balance Glute Kickback

reference.title: Resistance Band Standing Balance Glute Kickback (version 2)
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.

equipment: Resistance band (mini loop above the knees)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the leg drives back, inhale as it returns.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s back, 0.5 s squeeze, 1.8 s forward

prescription.progression: Stronger band or a longer squeeze

cues.text: Band above the knees; hinge into a quarter squat on the left leg, hands on the hips.
Breathe out and drive the right knee back against the band.
Squeeze the glute; ribs down, no low-back arch.
Breathe in and bring the knee back under the hip slowly.
Stay balanced in the squat; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to kick higher
mistakes.fix: Stop when the hip is fully open; the range is small.

mistakes.mistake: Standing up out of the squat

mistakes.fix: Pause at the back and return slower.
Keep both hip bones facing the floor.

kinematics.norm: Hip to about 10-20 degrees of extension past neutral; with the trunk hinged the thigh ends well behind vertical (clinical opinion); hip extension exercises excite the gluteus maximus (Macadam 2019; Neto 2020)
Quarter squat, trunk hinged about 25 degrees (clinical opinion)
Mini loop above the knees (elastic resistance, Andersen 2010)
Controlled, squeeze at the back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #18906, Resistance Band Standing Balance Glute Kickback (version 2), video (movement reference)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Krause Neto, Soares, Vieira et al. 2020, gluteus maximus activation during common strength and hypertrophy exercises: a systematic review (J Sports Sci Med 19(1):195-203)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjørnlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Check the band for nicks before use.
modify: Poor balance: one hand on a wall.
regressions: Standing hip extension without a band.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives hip extension against the band (Macadam 2019; Neto 2020).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on the stance leg (Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the stance hip in the quarter squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the stance knee bent (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Stops the low back arching (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lengthen at the back of the kick (clinical opinion).
